# Purpose

The MCDA baseline of the paper (Section 4.9) ranks the five corrective actions with TOPSIS,
the decision rule of the companion HMM pipeline. A reader may ask whether the gap between
this baseline and the POMDP is specific to TOPSIS. This notebook keeps everything else in the
MCDA controller fixed (the five criteria and their weights, the exponential smoothing of the
decoder labels, the Nominal override and the 0.5 s dwell time) and replaces only the
ranking method with three widely used methods from the RMCDA package, each from a different
family (additive weighting, compromise ranking and outranking):

| Method | RMCDA function | Score used (higher = better) |
|---|---|---|
| TOPSIS (paper) | `apply.TOPSIS` | closeness to the ideal solution |
| SAW (simple additive weighting) | `apply.SAW` | weighted sum of the normalised criteria |
| VIKOR | `apply.VIKOR` | $-Q_i$ (VIKOR ranks by smallest $Q_i$, with $\nu = 0.5$) |
| PROMETHEE II | `apply.PROMETHEE` | net outranking flow |

All controllers are evaluated with the per-sample simulator of the paper
(`R/sim_persample.R`): trajectories of 20 s start in Nominal, and trajectory $n$ of every
method uses `set.seed(700000 + n)`, the seeds of Table 5. The methods therefore face the same
random numbers, and their returns can be compared pairwise.

```{r load}
source(file.path(root, "R", "paths.R"))
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ load_core(); library(RMCDA); library(ggplot2); library(scales) })
```

# Decision matrix

The criteria are those of `mcda_topsis_action()` in `R/sim_persample.R` (Supplementary
Section S5.6). Three benefit criteria depend on the smoothed label distribution
$\hat p = (\hat p_N, \hat p_S, \hat p_D, \hat p_R)$; the stability penalty and the action cost
are fixed per action. The paper's TOPSIS call treats every column as a benefit and enters the
two costs as negative numbers. VIKOR and PROMETHEE in RMCDA make the same assumption, so they
receive the same matrix. SAW takes the costs as positive numbers together with
`beneficial.vector = 1:3`.

```{r criteria}
mcda_actions <- c("DwSensorA", "DwSensorB", "IncFilter", "ReidentPlant", "BiasCorrect")
stability_penalty <- c(0.08, 0.08, 0.05, 0.15, 0.12)
action_cost       <- c(0.10, 0.10, 0.15, 0.40, 0.25)
mcda_weights      <- c(0.35, 0.25, 0.15, 0.10, 0.15)

benefit_criteria <- function(p) {
  pN <- p[1]; pS <- p[2]; pD <- p[3]; pR <- p[4]
  sensor_n <- pS; plant_n <- pD; drift_n <- pR; kpi_n <- 1 - pN; noise_n <- sensor_n
  cbind(KPI_gain = c(pS * kpi_n * sensor_n * 1.2, pS * kpi_n * sensor_n * 0.6,
                     pS * kpi_n * noise_n, pD * kpi_n * plant_n,
                     (pR + 0.5 * pD) * kpi_n * (drift_n + 0.3 * plant_n)),
        Module_gain = c(pS * sensor_n * 1.2, pS * sensor_n * 0.6, pS * sensor_n * noise_n,
                        pD * plant_n, (pR + 0.5 * pD) * (drift_n + 0.3 * plant_n)),
        Drift_gain = c(pS * drift_n * 1.1, pS * drift_n * 0.7, pS * drift_n * 0.6,
                       pD * drift_n * 0.4, (pR + 0.2 * pS) * drift_n))
}
dm_negcost <- function(p) {   # costs as negative benefits (TOPSIS, VIKOR, PROMETHEE)
  m <- cbind(benefit_criteria(p), Stability = -stability_penalty, Cost = -action_cost)
  rownames(m) <- mcda_actions; m
}
dm_poscost <- function(p) {   # costs as positive values, with beneficial.vector = 1:3
  m <- cbind(benefit_criteria(p), Stability = stability_penalty, Cost = action_cost)
  rownames(m) <- mcda_actions; m
}

w <- mcda_weights
scorers <- list(
  "TOPSIS"       = function(p) as.numeric(apply.TOPSIS(dm_negcost(p), w = w)),
  "SAW"          = function(p) as.numeric(apply.SAW(dm_poscost(p), w, 1:3)[[1]]),
  "VIKOR"        = function(p) -as.numeric(apply.VIKOR(dm_negcost(p), w)[[2]][mcda_actions]),
  "PROMETHEE II" = function(p) as.numeric(apply.PROMETHEE(dm_negcost(p), w)[[3]])
)
```

Each score is turned into an action in the same way as in the paper's controller. If the
scores are undefined, the controller applies NoAction. This happens with every method when a
benefit column is zero for all five actions, for example before the first Drift label has
been decoded, because each method normalises the columns. If the smoothed probability of
Nominal exceeds 0.75, the controller also applies NoAction.

```{r action}
mcda_action_with <- function(scorer) function(p) {
  sc <- tryCatch(suppressWarnings(scorer(p)), error = function(e) rep(NA_real_, 5))
  desired <- if (all(!is.finite(sc))) "NoAction" else mcda_actions[which.max(sc)]
  if ((1 - p[1]) < 0.25 && p[1] > 0.75) desired <- "NoAction"
  desired
}
```

As a check, the TOPSIS version reproduces `mcda_topsis_action()` of the paper on 5,000 random
label distributions:

```{r check-topsis}
set.seed(1)
P <- matrix(rexp(4 * 5000), ncol = 4); P <- P / rowSums(P)
P[sample(5000, 1000), 4] <- 0; P <- P / rowSums(P)   # include distributions without Drift mass
topsis_act <- mcda_action_with(scorers[["TOPSIS"]])
all(apply(P, 1, topsis_act) == apply(P, 1, mcda_topsis_action))
```

How often does each method choose the same action as TOPSIS on these distributions?

```{r agreement}
acts <- sapply(names(scorers), function(m) apply(P, 1, mcda_action_with(scorers[[m]])))
round(colMeans(acts == acts[, "TOPSIS"]), 3)
```

# Closed-loop comparison

The controller below is `ctl_mcda()` of `R/sim_persample.R` with the ranking step passed in.
The simulation of the four methods takes several minutes; the results are cached in
`output/analyses/mcda_methods_runs.rds`. Delete that file to re-run them.

```{r controller}
ctl_mcda_with <- function(choose, dwell_sec = mcda_dwell_time, alpha_ema = 0.3) {
  list(init = function(s0, O_true) {
         e <- new.env(); e$p <- numeric(K)
         e$p[sample.int(K, 1L, prob = O_true[s0, ])] <- 1
         e$a <- "NoAction"; e$t_sw <- 0; e
       },
       act = function(st, s) st$a,
       update = function(st, a, z, t) {
         ind <- numeric(K); ind[z] <- 1
         st$p <- alpha_ema * ind + (1 - alpha_ema) * st$p; st$p <- st$p / sum(st$p)
         want <- choose(st$p)
         if (want != st$a && (t - st$t_sw) >= dwell_sec - 1e-9) { st$a <- want; st$t_sw <- t }
         st
       })
}

mismatch_rate <- function(tr, mdp_policy, T_end) {   # as in analyses/table5_final.R
  n <- length(tr$times); wrong <- 0
  for (i in seq_len(n - 1))
    if (tr$actions[i] != mdp_policy[states[tr$states[i]]]) wrong <- wrong + (tr$times[i + 1] - tr$times[i])
  if (tr$actions[n] != mdp_policy[states[tr$states[n]]]) wrong <- wrong + (T_end - tr$times[n])
  wrong / T_end
}
```

```{r simulate}
N <- nq(500, 50); T_end <- 20; seed0 <- 700000
cache <- out_path("analyses", "mcda_methods_runs.rds")
if (file.exists(cache) && identical(readRDS(cache)$N, N)) {
  runs <- readRDS(cache)$runs
} else {
  runs <- lapply(names(scorers), function(m) {
    ctl <- ctl_mcda_with(mcda_action_with(scorers[[m]]))
    r <- t(sapply(seq_len(N), function(n) {
      set.seed(seed0 + n)
      tr <- sim_ps(ctl, A, O_mat, s0 = 1L, T_end = T_end)
      c(ret = tr$disc_return, frac = frac_in_nominal(tr, T_end),
        mism = mismatch_rate(tr, vi$policy, T_end))
    }))
    data.frame(method = m, n = seq_len(N), r)
  })
  names(runs) <- names(scorers)
  saveRDS(list(N = N, runs = runs), cache)
}
```

The TOPSIS runs use the seeds of Table 5, so their returns must equal the first `r N` MCDA
returns of `analyses/table5_final.R`:

```{r check-table5}
t5 <- out_path("table5_final", "returns_per_trajectory.csv")
if (file.exists(t5)) {
  ref <- read.csv(t5, check.names = FALSE)[["MCDA (TOPSIS)"]][seq_len(N)]
  isTRUE(all.equal(runs[["TOPSIS"]]$ret, ref))
} else "Table 5 output not found (run Rscript run_all.R --only=table5)"
```

# Results

```{r summary}
summ <- do.call(rbind, lapply(runs, function(d) data.frame(
  Method = d$method[1], MeanReturn = mean(d$ret), SE = sd(d$ret) / sqrt(nrow(d)),
  FracNominal = mean(d$frac), MismatchPct = 100 * mean(d$mism))))
diffs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(runs), function(m) {
  d <- runs[[m]]$ret - runs[["TOPSIS"]]$ret
  p <- if (m == "TOPSIS" || all(d == 0)) NA_real_ else
    suppressWarnings(wilcox.test(d, mu = 0, exact = FALSE)$p.value)
  data.frame(Method = m, DiffVsTOPSIS = mean(d), DiffSE = sd(d) / sqrt(length(d)), Wilcoxon_p = p)
}))
summ <- merge(summ, diffs, by = "Method")
summ <- summ[order(-summ$MeanReturn), ]
summ$Wilcoxon_p_Holm <- p.adjust(summ$Wilcoxon_p, method = "holm")
knitr::kable(summ, digits = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 1, 1, 2, 4, 4), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = sprintf("Mean discounted return over %d trajectories of 20 s. DiffVsTOPSIS: mean paired difference in return from TOPSIS (same seeds); Wilcoxon signed-rank p-values, Holm-adjusted over the three comparisons.", N))
```

For reference, the other policies of Table 5 (2,000 trajectories each):

```{r reference}
tb_file <- out_path("table5_final", "PolicySummaryTable.csv")
ref_pol <- c("Optimal MDP", "POMDP (PBVI)", "Myopic belief", "MCDA (TOPSIS)", "No Intervention")
tb <- if (file.exists(tb_file)) read.csv(tb_file) else NULL
if (!is.null(tb)) knitr::kable(tb[tb$Policy %in% ref_pol, c("Policy", "MeanReward", "SEReward", "FracNominal", "MismatchPct")],
                               digits = c(0, 1, 2, 3, 1), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r plot, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.6}
summ$Method <- factor(summ$Method, levels = rev(summ$Method))
p <- ggplot(summ, aes(MeanReturn, Method)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = MeanReturn - 1.96 * SE, xmax = MeanReturn + 1.96 * SE),
                 height = 0.2, colour = "#5A7863") +
  geom_point(size = 2.6, colour = "#5A7863") +
  labs(x = "Mean discounted return (95% CI)", y = NULL,
       title = "MCDA decision layer with different ranking methods") +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
        axis.text = element_text(size = 11.5, colour = "black"), axis.title = element_text(size = 12.5))
if (!is.null(tb)) {
  refs <- tb[tb$Policy %in% c("Optimal MDP", "POMDP (PBVI)", "No Intervention"), ]
  p <- p + geom_vline(data = refs, aes(xintercept = MeanReward), linetype = "dashed",
                      colour = c("#213C51", "#574964", "darkred")[match(refs$Policy,
                               c("Optimal MDP", "POMDP (PBVI)", "No Intervention"))]) +
    geom_text(data = refs, aes(x = MeanReward, y = 0.45, label = Policy), inherit.aes = FALSE,
              angle = 90, hjust = 0, vjust = -0.4, size = 3.3)
}
p
```

# Reading the results

The table and the plot answer one question: does any of these ranking rules, given the same
smoothed labels, criteria and weights, close the gap to the POMDP? All of them score each
decision epoch on its own and ignore the regime dynamics and the reliability of the decoder,
so differences between them come only from how they aggregate the five criteria. The paired
differences show whether a method differs from TOPSIS by more than the Monte Carlo noise, and
the dashed lines place every method relative to the POMDP, the MDP and No Intervention.

In this run the mean returns of the four methods lie between
`r sprintf("%.1f", min(summ$MeanReturn))` and `r sprintf("%.1f", max(summ$MeanReturn))`,
none of the three alternatives differs from TOPSIS at the 5% level after the Holm adjustment
(smallest adjusted p-value `r sprintf("%.2f", min(summ$Wilcoxon_p_Holm, na.rm = TRUE))`), and
all of them remain far below the POMDP. Although the methods pick a different action from
TOPSIS on some label distributions, in closed loop they lead to almost the same behaviour. The
gap reported in the paper therefore reflects the per-epoch, label-driven design of the MCDA
controller, and the choice of TOPSIS within that design has little effect on it.
